subtitle: Analyze, predict, and generate: pandas for storefront data, scikit-learn basics for churn and basket analysis, then a GenAI layer — Python end to end for e-commerce
audience: Developers who can write basic Python loops and functions and now do real data work: cleaning order CSVs, aggregating sales, training a first churn model, and wrapping results in guarded natural-language answers. Python 3.10+ with pandas 2.x and scikit-learn 1.x (verified locally during authoring); JavaScript logic-twins run in the playground where the platform needs runnable cells.
outcomes: Set up reproducible Python projects (venvs, pinned requirements, env vars, logging, layout)
Load, inspect, and slice e-commerce CSVs with pandas (read_csv, head/info/describe, filtering, sorting)
Clean real mess: missing values, duplicates, types, dates, and currency strings — with quarantine discipline
Aggregate with groupby (sales by category/country, pivots, time resampling) and verify totals reconcile
Join orders/customers/products and engineer RFM-style features without leakage
Train and evaluate a first churn classifier (split, logistic regression, precision/recall) honestly
Mine basket co-occurrence pairs and evaluate them against holdout baskets
Wrap analysis in a guarded GenAI layer (templated answers, cited numbers, abstention paths)

assessment.q: CSV loads with prices as '$129.00' strings and dates as mixed formats. Order of operations?
options: Parse types on load (dtype/converters), standardize dates/currency explicitly, quarantine unparseable rows with reasons — types before analysis
assessment.explain: Analysis on strings silently corrupts (sorting '$100' > '$20' lexicographically). Types first, with quarantine for the unparseable (Ch.2–3).

assessment.q: groupby totals don't match the raw row count. First check?
options: Join fanout or dropped NaN groups: verify merge cardinality (validate='many_to_one') and dropna behavior before trusting aggregates
assessment.explain: Totals must reconcile: fanout multiplies, NaN keys vanish silently. Merge validation + count reconciliation prove aggregates (Ch.4–5).

assessment.q: Churn model scores 0.97 accuracy with 4% churn rate. Verdict?
options: Suspicious: majority-class baseline is 0.96 — report precision/recall/F1 per class and beat a dummy classifier, not accuracy
assessment.explain: Imbalanced accuracy lies by default. Precision/recall per class plus dummy baselines separate signal from majority-vote theater (Ch.6).

assessment.q: Features include 'days_since_last_order' computed on full history including the prediction window. Problem?
options: Leakage: future information in training features inflates scores that collapse live — cut features at the decision point (as-of joins)
assessment.explain: Leakage is the silent killer of ML evals: features must reflect only pre-decision knowledge. As-of discipline, always (Ch.5–6).

assessment.q: Basket rule 'buys X → buys Y' has high confidence but support 2. Action?
options: Demand support thresholds: high-confidence rare rules are noise — support × confidence gates, validated on holdout baskets
assessment.explain: Confidence without support is anecdote with math. Holdout validation separates patterns from coincidences (Ch.7).

assessment.q: GenAI summary states a revenue figure not in the analysis output. Fix layer?
options: Grounded generation contract: numbers only from computed tables with citations; anything else abstains — same grounding discipline as RAG
assessment.explain: Generated numbers must trace to computed cells. Scope-to-tables contracts plus abstention paths (Ch.8).

assessment.q: requirements.txt unpinned, CI installs latest. Risk?
options: Drift breakage: unpinned pandas/sklearn shift APIs quarterly — pin versions, lock files, verify in CI
assessment.explain: Reproducibility demands pins: unpinned data-stack deps break quarterly. Lock + verify (Ch.1).

assessment.q: Duplicate order rows inflate revenue 2x. Prevention order?
options: Dedupe on declared keys (order_id) with provenance before aggregating — duplicates corrupt every downstream number
assessment.explain: Key-based dedupe with provenance precedes all aggregation. Doubled inputs double every output silently (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Timezone-naive vs aware timestamps mixed in orders. Rule?
options: Normalize to UTC ISO on ingest, reject ambiguous, quarantine unparseable — time math on mixed zones silently shifts
assessment.explain: Mixed-zone arithmetic shifts silently across DST/boundaries. Canonical UTC on ingest with quarantine for ambiguity (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Notebook-only analysis handed to production. Gaps?
options: Scripts + tests + logging + pinned env + scheduled runs: production needs modules, contracts, and observability, not cells
assessment.explain: Notebook-to-production gap: modular code, tested functions, logged runs, pinned envs, scheduled execution. Cells don't operate (Ch.1 + capstone).

project.title: The Store Analyst Pack
project.summary: Deliver a reproducible Python pack over a real order CSV (1000+ rows, yours or provided): cleaned dataset with quarantine report, sales aggregation notebook-turned-script with reconciled totals, a churn classifier with honest metrics vs dummy baselines, basket rules validated on holdout, and a GenAI summary layer with cited numbers — all pinned, tested, and runnable end to end.
requirements: Reproducible env: venv, pinned requirements, .env config, logging, module layout (no notebook-only)
Cleaned CSV + quarantine report (per-rule reject counts with reasons)
Aggregation script: sales by category/country/month with totals reconciled to raw counts
Churn model: as-of features, train/test split, precision/recall/F1 vs dummy baselines, leakage statement
Basket rules with support/confidence gates validated on holdout baskets
GenAI layer: templated answers citing computed cells, abstention paths, evaluation on 10 questions
technical: Python 3.10+, pandas 2.x, scikit-learn 1.x pinned; all snippets executed during authoring
Playground JS twins mirror core logic (groupby/aggregation shapes) for in-platform runs
Tests for cleaning rules and aggregation reconciliation; logging on every run
Numbers reproducible: seeds fixed, datasets versioned, parameters committed
project.architecture: Five sections: (1) Data dossier — sources, shapes, quality findings; (2) Cleaning — rules, quarantine taxonomy, reject rates; (3) Analysis — aggregations with reconciliations; (4) Modeling — features (as-of!), metrics vs dummies, leakage statement; (5) GenAI layer — contracts, citations, eval scores.
steps: Scaffold env + layout; load and profile the CSV (shapes, dtypes, nulls, dupes)
Clean with rules + quarantine; reconcile counts at every stage
Aggregate (category/country/month) with total reconciliation; engineer as-of features
Train churn model vs dummy baselines; write the leakage statement explicitly
Mine basket rules with gates; validate on holdout; wrap in GenAI layer with citations
Assemble the pack with README (run order), tests green, numbers reproducible
evaluation: Reconciliation holds at every stage (raw → clean → aggregated → modeled)
Model beats dummy baselines on precision/recall (not just accuracy); leakage statement present
Basket rules gated and holdout-validated; GenAI answers cite computed cells or abstain
Env reproducible from scratch (pinned); tests pass; logs complete
stretch: Add a price-elasticity slice (cohort analysis with confidence intervals)
Schedule weekly runs with drift alerts on schema/shape changes
Serve one endpoint (FastAPI) exposing the churn score with contract tests

interviewQs.q: Groupby totals don't reconcile with raw counts. Debug order?
interviewQs.a: Check join fanout first (merge validate='many_to_one' + pre/post counts), then NaN group keys (dropped silently — decide fill vs drop explicitly), then duplicate keys, then dtype surprises (string prices sorting lexicographically). Reconciliation is staged: raw → clean → joined → aggregated counts must chain consistently, and the break names the culprit.

No-go on accuracy alone: dummy majority baseline is 0.96. Demand precision/recall/F1 per class plus lift over dummy, then check leakage (as-of features?), then calibration (do 0.8s convert ~80%?). Accuracy on imbalanced data is a vanity metric; decisions need per-class truth plus leakage statements.

interviewQs.q: Feature uses full-history recency including the outcome window. Issue?
interviewQs.a: Leakage: training sees post-decision information unavailable at prediction time — scores inflate, live performance collapses. Fix with as-of joins (features computed strictly before each decision point) and state the cutoff rule explicitly. Every feature needs a timestamp discipline, reviewed like code.

interviewQs.q: Mixed timezones and '$1,234.56' vs '1.234,56' in one CSV. Approach?
interviewQs.a: Canonicalize on ingest: datetimes to UTC ISO (reject ambiguous, quarantine unparseable), money to Decimal/plain floats with explicit locale policy per column (never blind comma-strip). Parsing rules stated, failures quarantined with reasons, samples verified. Locale ambiguity resolved by documented corpus convention, never guessed per row.

interviewQs.q: Notebook analysis to production — what's missing?
interviewQs.a: Modularity (functions/modules, not cells), contracts (typed I/O), tests (cleaning rules, reconciliations), logging (per-run records), pinned envs, scheduling (cron/jobs with drift alerts), and review (versioned code). Notebooks explore; production operates — the gap is engineering discipline around identical logic.

interviewQs.q: GenAI summary of analysis states uncomputed figures. Fix layer?
interviewQs.a: Grounding contract: numbers only from computed tables with cell citations; anything else abstains with a stated gap. Same discipline as RAG generation (scope-to-context, per-claim citations, staleness awareness). Fix the contract and add gold questions asserting citation presence — prompt tuning without contracts repeats the failure.
